answer: Layered shale, not a single gate, sets standing. An identity earns each layer by completed work that two unrelated observers already logged, and a layer can only be added on top of one the same cluster already holds, so aliases cannot leap ahead. Every added layer emits a pulse priced by depth: the k-th layer an operator stacks costs k squared in escrow, so n heads need about n cubed and every head still requires fresh outsiders. Reputation then decays on a spiral, each epoch discounting a fixed fraction unless new audited work lands, so stockpiled layers cannot carry a silent cluster.
